How does the RNA helicase UPF1 control nuclear gene expression?

School of Biosciences, University of Birmingham

  • Supervisor: Dr Saverio Brogna (s.brogna@bham.ac.uk)
  • Application deadline: 15 January 2027

This PhD project will investigate how UPF1 coordinates transcription and RNA processing in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Help people understand medicine and biology through the science you care about. Create conversations and short videos that explore how researchers investigate a question, what the evidence reveals, and what remains uncertain.

The Immune-Aging Project’s Communication Fellowship helps you develop and publish this work—with mentoring, scientific and editorial feedback, and production support. For people studying or working in medicine and the life sciences.

  • Remote · 4 hours/week · 3 months
  • The weekly commitment includes 1.5–2 hours of mentoring and group meetings.<

item.content:encoded: We are seeking a highly motivated early-career researcher to apply with us for the upcoming Juan de la Cierva postdoctoral fellowship, funded by the Spanish National Research Agency (AEI). This is a prestigious, competitive scheme aimed at researchers within three years of their PhD who show clear potential for an independent scientific trajectory.
